summary: Depression-era stone fire tower near Cornelia, Georgia, staffed again since 1989 and now maintained by a local volunteer group.

facts.design: 40-foot stone tower with 14x14-foot wood cab and peaked slate roof

staffing.status: staffed seasonally by Georgia Forestry Commission

access.note: No source consulted states current public access or climbing rules.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Chattahoochee National Forest); staffed by Georgia Forestry Commission

events.note: NHLR gives 1936, built by the WPA
Wikipedia gives 1937, attributing construction to the Resettlement Administration
Tower formally dedicated June 7, 1938, with Governor Eurith D. Rivers speaking
Wikipedia gives June 11, 1984 for NRHP listing (ref 84001110)
Georgia Forestry Commission resumed seasonal staffing
Registered on National Historic Lookout Register December 1, 1998

evidence.supports: WPA built it in 1936 for Chattahoochee National Forest
evidence.quote: A classic design built by the Works Progress Administration (WPA) in 1936 for the Chattahoochee National Forest

evidence.supports: 40-foot stone tower with 14x14 cab and slate roof
evidence.quote: Chenocetah Mountain Lookout, is a 40' high stone tower with a 14' x 14' wood cab covered by a 15' high peaked slate roof

evidence.supports: Dedicated after WWII to three forest workers who died
evidence.quote: After World War II it was dedicated to three forest workers who died during the war.

evidence.supports: Active until 1975, unused until 1989 when GFC took over staffing
evidence.quote: In active service until 1975, it was unused until 1989 when the Georgia Forestry Commission took over staffing during fire season.
The tower has been adopted by neighbors living in residential areas near the mountain who have formed the “Chenocetah Conservation Corps” to provide grounds maintenance.
It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1983.

evidence.supports: Built in 1937 by the Resettlement Administration
evidence.quote: The tower was built in 1937 as part of a public works program by the Farm Security Administration's Resettlement Administration
The stone tower measures 40 feet (12 m) tall and was first dedicated on June 7, 1938. Governor Eurith D. Rivers delivered the dedicatory address

evidence.supports: Rededicated after WWII to three forest workers
evidence.quote: The tower was dedicated again after World War II in memory of three forest workers who died during the war.

evidence.supports: Used until 1975, unused until 1989 GFC staffing
evidence.quote: The tower was used in active service as a fire tower until 1975. After 1975, it was unused until 1989 when the Georgia Forestry Commission took over staffing during the fire season.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 1936 (attributing construction to the WPA); Wikipedia gives 1937 (attributing it to the Resettlement Administration) with formal dedication in 1938. Both are reported in the story.
NHLR gives 1983; Wikipedia gives June 11, 1984. Both are reported in the story.

notes_for_editor: Current public access/climbing status is not documented in either source; worth a follow-up with the Chattahoochee National Forest or GFC. Build-year and NRHP-listing-year conflicts between the two sources are noted but not resolved.
